analysis.title: Weekly Market Guide
key_insights: The S&P 500 has moved sideways for the past few months. Strong fundamentals were offset by higher oil prices and interest rates.

On Nov 4, a Democratic House and Senate sweep had the equal-weighted 'average stock' trading to new highs, on lower oil prices tied to a 'potential end to the Iran war'. Stocks levered to the AI buildout and Energy lagged.
The firm cautions against knee-jerk reactions to election outcomes. Politics rarely changes long-term fundamentals overnight, and early market reactions have often reversed or proven wrong.

Past election reactions reversed: after 2016 Tech was among the worst initial reactions and then the best performer over 12 and 24 months, while Energy was among the best initial reactions and then the worst over 1-2 years.

After the 2020 election, Energy and Banks had weak initial reactions, then were the two best performers over the next 12 months, helped by a Covid vaccine and reopening optimism. Health Care was an initial winner and then lagged.
After the 2022 midterms every sector fell on day 1 (Tech -2.6%), then AI took shape in early 2023. After the 2018 midterms the broad rally weakened quickly.

After the 2024 election Consumer Discretionary rose 22% over the first 31 days but is at about the same level nearly two years later. Financials rose 6.2% on day 1 and did not sustain outperformance over the next year. Consumer Discretionary is the best sector again on this election day, and the firm asks whether it will sustain.

Q3 earnings season: 68% of S&P 500 companies have reported, 82% beat on EPS by an aggregate 2.7%. The 2.7% beat is well below Q1 and Q2, which were skewed by private investment mark-ups at mega-cap Tech+ names.

Operating earnings are strong with solid beat rates across sectors. Expected growth and estimate revisions remain positive. Several mega-cap Tech and Communication Services names fell on capex scrutiny and high expectations.

The firm says the overall environment remains positive for equities, with solid economic activity and strong earnings growth with positive forward revisions. It suggests assessing election 'winners' and 'losers' over the coming weeks for opportunities.
Technical breadth has firmed recently, which the firm calls supportive of market trends. The 'average stock' has see-sawed with interest rates and oil prices and broke out as both receded.

sector_views.rationale: Energy fell 5.2% on Nov 4 on lower oil on a potential end to the Iran war. Q3 EPS growth is estimated at 155.0% y/y, but 2027 EPS is estimated down 14.2%, and the firm notes Energy was a poor performer after the 2016 election.
Tech rose 0.9% on Nov 4, below the S&P 500's 1.7%. Q3 EPS growth is 65.1% y/y with a 6.0% surprise. AI-levered stocks lagged and semiconductors fell 2.6% on the day.
Best sector on Nov 4 at +4.8%, but the firm notes the sector surged after the 2024 election and then underperformed for nearly two years, and asks whether the move will sustain.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 earnings season: 68% of companies reported, 82% beat on EPS (reported figures, already printed) by an aggregate 2.7%. Q3 EPS growth is 28.6% y/y and -9.0% q/q.
Sector Q3 EPS surprise (reported): Communication Services -21.5%, Health Care +13.2%, Industrials +7.7%, Energy +7.2%, Information Technology +6.0%, Utilities +6.0%.
Estimated EPS growth (consensus): S&P 500 2026 +16.4%, 2027 +17.2%. Information Technology 2026 +42.3%, 2027 +27.0%. Energy 2026 -8.5%, 2027 -14.2%.
Estimate changes since 9/30/26 for the S&P 500: Q3'26 +1.6%, 2026 +0.8%, 2027 +1.7%, 2028 +1.7%. Energy rose most: +16.3% for Q3'26 and +10.1% for 2026.
risk_factors: Higher oil prices and higher interest rates have capped S&P 500 gains in recent months.
Capex scrutiny and high expectations have pressured several mega-cap Tech and Communication Services names after earnings.
Initial election-driven sector moves have historically reversed, so positioning on them carries reversal risk.
vol_and_positioning: Technical breadth has firmed recently, with the equal-weighted S&P 500 breaking out to new highs on Nov 4 as interest rates and oil prices receded.
geopolitical: A 'potential end to the Iran war' lowered oil prices on Nov 4 and drove the equal-weighted S&P 500 to new highs while Energy fell 5.2%.
US election outcome: a Democratic sweep of the House and Senate, as named in the report.

tension_points.bull_case: The equal-weighted S&P 500 broke out to new highs on lower oil prices and rates, and technical breadth has firmed. Consumer Discretionary led at +4.8% on Nov 4.
tension_points.bear_case: Initial election reactions have often reversed or proven wrong: Tech and Energy in 2016, Energy and Banks in 2020, Consumer Discretionary after 2024.
